D.t: Helena Foulkes leads by 13.8 in the forecast and wins 99% of simulations. The cushion is about 58,767 votes; a one point swing is about 2,129 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +7.0 and D +20.3. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is D +8.6. Your best recent poll is University of New Hampshire at D +19.2; your worst is Emerson College/WPRI at D +9.7. 5 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Providence, a projected net 36,761 votes; Newport, a projected net 9,973 votes; Bristol, a projected net 6,862 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Kent, R +1.8, 18.0% of the vote; Washington, D +10.2, 15.2% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Helena Foulkes runs furthest behind in Washington, Kent. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 86% of voters, 48 to 37, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.28 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 64% of voters, 52 to 33, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.19 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 64% of voters, 52 to 33, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.18 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Helena Foulkes: Immigration voters 17 to 59, Independents 43 to 43, Men 43 to 40. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
$215K cash against $264K. Roughly even money; the air war will be decided by outside groups and earned media.
Registered Democrats cast 44% of the 92,353 ballots in Rhode Island so far, against 9% for the other party. That is 10.4 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.
